LESSON: LISTENING AND SPEAKING 1.1.1 POLITE LANGUAGE: TELEPHONE ETIQUETTE

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 8
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 1
Topic 1.1: Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Polite Language: Telephone Etiquette
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Polite Language: Telephone Etiquette, part of Strand 1 in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 8 ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: Why should one be polite when speaking over the telephone? 2. How do you conduct a telephone conversation using polite words and expressions?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Polite Language: Telephone Etiquette together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Communication as the learner speaks with clarity while carrying out telephone conversations.

● Digital literacy as the learner uses the telephone to make calls under the guidance of the teacher.

Values:
Respect is enhanced as learners take turns during telephone conversations role-play

Link to other subjects:

Using polite words to communicate over the phone is linked to communication in all subjects.
